about: generated artifacts and third-party provenance and licences, complete.
Complete means every file a downstream branch receives can be traced to
something that produced it and to a licence that permits it to be
there. Versions are not restated here where spec/r1_toolchain.lock.json
already pins them -- a second copy of a version number is a second
thing to forget to update -- so entries point at the lock instead.

build_tools.note: a simulator, not a library. Nothing it produces is distributed and nothing links against it, so its licence does not reach the export.
analysis only at this stage; no netlist it produces is shipped.
build_tools.role: structural checking and the synthesis proxy

build_tools.note: OPTIONAL. The generated Verilog is checked in, so a build without XLS produces the same export; XLS is needed only to regenerate it.

compile_dependencies.note: an installed wheel, never a working tree. tools/r35/upstream_tests.py R35-UP-01 refuses an editable install.
compile_dependencies.used_for: the TTIR frontend, the LinearLayout algebra and the canonicalize/CSE pipeline

generated_artifacts.why_checked_in: so the RTL builds and the export ships without XLS installed. doc/xls.md has the regeneration workflow.

generated_artifacts.generated_from: spec/, isa/, compiler/targets/, rtl/, tb/common/, tb/device/
generated_artifacts.why_not_checked_in: it is a copy of files that are already in the tree. It is in .gitignore and rebuilt from a stamp with prerequisites, because a stale copy of the RTL is worse than no copy: the runtime reads it in preference to the working tree.

generated_artifacts.note: the hardware export. Its own MANIFEST.json lists every file with a hash.

integrity.how: every file listed in MANIFEST.json is re-hashed and compared, with the tree made read-only first, so the check cannot be the thing that repairs it.

about: R36-BUILD-03 asks for two independent clean builds to be comparable,
with the normalisation rules declared in advance rather than
discovered when the comparison fails. These are the fields that may
differ between two builds of the same source and still mean the same
thing. Everything NOT listed here must match byte for byte.
normalisation.content_normalisation: none. No file in the export contains a timestamp, a build host or an absolute path, and the comparison would catch it if one did.

why.source_commit: a clean build from an archive has no commit. Two builds of the same source must agree on the FILES, which is what the hashes are for.
why.tools: the iverilog and yosys version strings of the machine that ran the build. They record the environment, not the artifact.

runtime_dependencies.note: the Python standard library only. An artifact loads and runs in an environment with no Triton, no MLIR, no compiler and no assembler -- R36-BUILD-02 shows it by installing the wheel into a fresh environment, DELETING tnca_cc and the assembler modules from it, and running an artifact compiled elsewhere. The wheel ships both halves on purpose (pyproject's packages.find takes tnca* and tnca_cc*), so the claim is about dependence, not about absence.
